examples.en: If you spend money carelessly, it's gone quickly.
I'm sorry for losing my temper without thinking.
You shouldn't believe rumors without discernment.
He recklessly talked about other people's secrets.
The kids are running around recklessly, which is dangerous.
Don't make promises without thinking.

explain: 앞뒤를 따져 보지 않고 행동한다는 느낌이에요. '함부로'와 비슷한데, '함부로'가 더 일상적이고 '분별없이'는 조금 딱딱해요. '쓰다, 믿다, 말하다, 행동하다' 같은 동사와 자주 어울려요.

phrases.example: 남의 물건을 함부로 만지면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't touch other people's things carelessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분별없이'와 비슷하지만 더 일상적이어서 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 분별없이 but more everyday, so it is common in speech.

phrases.en: You end up regretting thoughtless behavior later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분별없다'를 '-는'으로 바꿔서 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adjective form 분별없다 used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 생각 없이 말하면 친구가 상처받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you speak without thinking, your friend may get hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분별없이'보다 쉽고 편한 말이라 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more casual way to say it, common in conversation.

explain_en: It gives the feeling of acting without weighing things up. It is similar to '함부로', but '함부로' is more everyday and '분별없이' is a bit stiffer. It pairs often with verbs like '쓰다', '믿다', '말하다' and '행동하다'.

en: to be exhausted; to be used up

examples.en: This year's budget has all been used up.

examples.ko: 하루 일을 마치니 체력이 다 소진됐어요.
examples.en: After finishing the day's work, my energy was completely drained.

examples.ko: 인기 상품은 며칠 만에 소진될 거예요.
examples.en: Popular items will run out within a few days.
The coupons ran out quickly, so I couldn't get one.
Charge it before the battery runs out.
I rested for a week to recover my depleted energy.

explain: 소진되다는 힘, 예산, 재고처럼 쓰는 것이 자연스럽게 모두 줄어서 없어질 때 써요. 내가 일부러 다 쓴 게 아니라 '그렇게 되었다'는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '다 떨어졌어요'가 더 흔하고, 공지나 뉴스에서 소진되다를 자주 봐요.

phrases.example: 인기 있는 표는 벌써 다 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: The popular tickets have already run out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 소진되다 대신 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural spoken alternative to 소진되다.

phrases.en: Stock of popular items runs out quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 모두 팔려 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when goods are all sold and gone.

phrases.en: Use the coupon before it runs out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 없어지기 전에 하라고 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to act before it is used up.

explain_en: Supplies, tickets, or energy get used up; formal, passive. Sojindoeda is used when energy, budget, or stock gradually gets fully used up, as a state that came about rather than something you did on purpose. In daily talk 다 떨어졌어요 is more common, while notices and news often use 소진되다.

t90.ax: Charge it before the battery runs out.

en: to be lost; to suffer loss

examples.en: The computer broke down, and the data was lost.
Some of the crops are lost because of the rain.

examples.ko: 손실된 금액은 보험으로 보상받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can be compensated by insurance for the lost amount.
Many cultural properties are lost to fires.

examples.ko: 열이 새 나가면 에너지가 손실될 거예요.
examples.en: If heat escapes, energy will be lost.

examples.ko: 파일이 손실되면 처음부터 다시 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: If the file is lost, you have to remake it from the start.

explain: 돈, 데이터, 에너지, 재산 같은 것이 줄어들거나 없어질 때 써요. '잃어버리다'는 내가 물건을 놓친 느낌이고 '손실되다'는 손해를 보는 객관적인 말이에요. 회사 보고서나 뉴스에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: The file suddenly disappeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '손실되다'보다 쉬운 말이라 일상에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 손실되다 for everyday use.

phrases.en: I found the lost data again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잃어버린 자료나 돈을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier for lost data or money.

phrases.en: Save in advance so the data isn't lost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손해가 생기지 않도록 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn someone to avoid losing something.

explain_en: Data, money or profit is lost as damage; not for a misplaced item. Used when something like money, data, energy or property decreases or disappears. 잃어버리다 feels like you personally lost an item, while 손실되다 is a more objective word for taking a loss. It is common in company reports and news.

t90.ax: If heat escapes, energy will be lost.

en: to lose one's footing; to miss one's step; to slip down

examples.en: I lost my footing on the trail while hiking and hurt my leg.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 계단에서 실족하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: It is easy to slip on stairs on rainy days.

examples.ko: 그는 바위에서 실족했지만 다행히 크게 다치지 않았어요.
examples.en: He lost his footing on a rock, but fortunately he was not badly hurt.
I almost lost my footing on the snowy road yesterday.
If you slip and fall in the mountains, call 119 right away.

examples.ko: 어두운 길에서 실족하지 않게 손전등을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I brought a flashlight so I would not slip on the dark path.

explain: 산길, 계단, 물가처럼 위험한 곳에서 발을 잘못 디뎌 넘어지거나 떨어질 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '발을 헛디디다'라고 더 자주 말하고, '실족하다'는 뉴스나 안전 안내문에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: I missed a step on the stairs and almost fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '실족하다'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech this is used more than 실족하다.

phrases.en: Slip-and-fall accidents often happen in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안전 안내에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in news and safety notices.

phrases.en: I lost my footing on the wet rock and fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서/-어서'로 이어 실족한 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links with -아서/-어서 to give the result of losing one's footing.

explain_en: Slip and fall by missing one's step; written or news style. It is used when you misstep and fall at dangerous places such as mountain trails, stairs or waterfronts. In daily conversation people more often say '발을 헛디디다', while '실족하다' appears a lot in the news and safety notices.

examples.ko: 약물 오용은 건강에 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: Drug misuse is a serious problem for your health.

examples.ko: 단어 오용 때문에 뜻이 이상하게 전달됐어요.
examples.en: The meaning came across strangely because of the misuse of a word.

examples.ko: 권한 오용으로 그 공무원은 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: That official was investigated for misuse of authority.

examples.ko: 항생제 오용을 막기 위해 의사의 처방이 필요해요.
examples.en: A doctor's prescription is needed to prevent the misuse of antibiotics.

examples.ko: 맞춤법에서 자주 보이는 오용 사례를 정리했어요.
examples.en: I put together common examples of misuse in spelling.

examples.ko: 장비 오용으로 사고가 난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was once an accident caused by the misuse of equipment.

explain: 약, 권한, 말처럼 쓰는 방법이 정해진 것을 틀리게 쓸 때 써요. '남용'은 지나치게 많이 쓴다는 쪽이라서 '오용'과 달라요.

phrases.example: 약을 오용하면 몸에 해로울 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Misusing medicine can be harmful to your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오용'에 '하다'를 붙여 틀리게 쓰는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하다' makes it the action of using something wrongly.

phrases.en: The person in charge apologized for misusing authority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 뉴스에서 힘이나 자격을 잘못 쓴 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in business or news for wrongly using power or authority.

phrases.en: This expression is often misused.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아닌 말이나 물건이 틀리게 쓰인다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or things are wrongly used by people.

explain_en: Using something wrongly or improperly, often by error (약 오용). It is used when something with a proper way of use, like medicine, authority or words, is used wrongly. '남용' (overuse) is about using too much, so it differs from '오용'.

t90.ax: Drug misuse is a serious problem for your health.

en: to break away from; to secede from

examples.en: The train went off the track.

examples.ko: 선수 한 명이 대열에서 이탈한 걸 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Nobody noticed that one player had dropped out of the line.
Leaving the path is dangerous, so follow the signs.

examples.ko: 비행기가 정해진 경로를 이탈하는 일은 드물어요.
examples.en: It is rare for a plane to leave its set route.
Customers keep leaving, so the company is worried.
I check every day so I don't stray from the plan.

explain: 정해진 길, 줄, 집단, 규칙에서 벗어나 떨어져 나갈 때 써요. 기차는 선로를, 선수는 대열을, 고객은 서비스를 이탈해요. '벗어나다'보다 딱딱하고 뉴스나 업무에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The car went off the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요. '이탈하다'는 뉴스나 업무에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday word; 이탈하다 is more for news and work.

phrases.example: 가격이 오르면 고객 이탈이 생길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If prices go up, customers may leave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 고객이 떠나는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun collocation for customers leaving a company.

phrases.en: Please do not leave the guide line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 길이나 규칙을 지키라고 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices telling people to stay on the set path or follow the rules.

explain_en: Use it when something leaves a set path, line, group or rule. A train leaves its track, a player leaves the formation, a customer leaves a service. It is stiffer than '벗어나다' and common in news and business.

en: to vanish; to disappear; to abscond

examples.ko: 그 연예인은 논란 뒤에 한동안 잠적했어요.
examples.en: That celebrity went into hiding for a while after the controversy.
Some people disappear because of their debts.

examples.ko: 사장이 갑자기 잠적해서 회사가 문을 닫았대요.
examples.en: I heard the boss suddenly vanished and the company closed down.
Nobody knows where he has gone into hiding.

examples.ko: 잠적하기 전에 한 번만이라도 연락해 주지 그랬어요?
examples.en: Why didn't you at least contact me once before you disappeared?

examples.ko: 한 달째 잠적한 친구에게서 드디어 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I finally got a text from my friend who had been out of contact for a month.

explain: 스스로 연락을 끊고 숨는 것이라서 '사라지다'보다 의도가 느껴져요. 보통 사람이나 연예인, 사장처럼 책임을 피하는 상황에서 뉴스에 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 약속 날에 친구가 갑자기 잠적해 버렸어요.
phrases.en: My friend suddenly vanished on the day of our appointment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 버리다'를 붙이면 놀랍거나 아쉬운 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 버리다' adds a feeling of surprise or regret.

phrases.en: He cut off contact and disappeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠적하는 방식을 더 분명하게 말하는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase that makes clear how the person disappeared.

phrases.en: The employees are looking for the boss who disappeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠적한'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 뉴스 같은 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form gives a news-like tone.

explain_en: It means cutting contact and hiding on one's own, so it carries more sense of intention than '사라지다'. It often appears in the news about people, celebrities or bosses who avoid responsibility.

en: to drop; to decline; to deteriorate

examples.en: Stamina declines as you get older.
I'm worried because my grades keep dropping.
When you lack sleep, your concentration tends to decline.
The temperature dropped suddenly and my condition got worse.
We exchange products whose quality has declined.

examples.ko: 학습 의욕이 저하되는 시기가 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has a time when their motivation to study drops.

explain: 저하되다는 능력, 성적, 품질, 의욕, 면역력처럼 좋아야 하는 수준이 내려갈 때 써요. 온도나 가격이 내려가는 일에는 '떨어지다', '내려가다'를 써요. 원인이 있어 낮아지게 하는 쪽은 '저하시키다'예요.

phrases.example: 요즘 잠을 못 자서 체력이 많이 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: I haven't been sleeping lately, so my stamina has dropped a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저하되다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 가격이나 온도에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 저하되다 but more natural in speech; it also works for prices and temperatures.

phrases.en: If you don't get enough sleep, your concentration declines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 나타내는 말과 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation with words for abilities.

phrases.example: 저하된 면역력을 높이려면 잘 먹고 푹 쉬어야 해요.
phrases.en: To raise a weakened immune system, you need to eat well and rest fully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저하되다'를 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형으로, 이미 낮아진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, describing a state that has already declined.

explain_en: Ability or quality gets lower; formal, passive form (집중력이 저하되다) 저하되다 is used when a level that ought to be good goes down, such as ability, grades, quality, motivation or immunity. For temperature or price going down use 떨어지다 or 내려가다. The causative form is 저하시키다.

t90.ax: Stamina declines as you get older.

examples.en: A hiker got stranded in the snow.

examples.ko: 조난 신고를 받고 구조대가 바로 출동했어요.
examples.en: The rescue team was dispatched right after receiving the distress report.

examples.ko: 안개가 심한 날에는 조난 위험이 커요.
examples.en: The risk of getting lost and in danger is high on very foggy days.

examples.ko: 조난 신호를 보내려고 휴대폰 손전등을 켰어요.
examples.en: I turned on my phone's flashlight to send a distress signal.

examples.ko: 조난 사고를 막으려면 혼자 산에 가지 마세요.
examples.en: To prevent people from getting stranded in accidents, don't go up the mountain alone.
A helicopter took off to look for the missing climber.

explain: 주로 등산, 바다, 눈보라 같은 자연 속 상황에서 쓰고 '조난(을) 당하다', '조난 신고/신호/사고'처럼 짝말로 나와요. 도시에서 일어난 사고에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스나 안전 안내에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I got lost in the mountains and was stranded in danger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조난'과 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 조난.

phrases.en: They sent a distress signal and the rescue team came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험할 때 도움을 구하려고 보내는 신호예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A signal sent to ask for help in danger.

phrases.example: 겨울 산에서는 조난 사고가 자주 나요.
phrases.en: Accidents where people get stranded often happen in the mountains in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안전 안내에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in news and safety notices.

explain_en: Getting stranded or in danger at sea or mountains. It is mainly used for situations in nature such as mountains, the sea and snowstorms, and comes in set phrases like '조난(을) 당하다' and '조난 신고/신호/사고'. It is not used for accidents in a city. You often see it in news and safety notices.

examples.ko: 작은 말다툼이 큰 싸움의 촉발이 됐어요.
examples.en: A small argument became the trigger for a big fight.
That incident was what set off the protest.
They are investigating the cause that set it off.
This announcement led to a controversy being set off.
Finding the triggering factor is important.
When was the point at which the economic crisis was set off?

explain: '~의 촉발', '촉발 원인'처럼 다른 말 앞뒤에 붙여 써요. 혼자 쓰기보다 동사 '촉발하다', '촉발되다'가 더 흔해요. 일상에서는 '계기'를 많이 쓰고, '촉발'은 뉴스·보고서 같은 딱딱한 글에서 써요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 사고의 촉발 원인을 조사하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The police are investigating what triggered the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 터지게 한 이유를 뉴스나 보고서에서 말할 때 '촉발'을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '촉발' placed before a noun to name the reason something broke out, in news or reports.

phrases.example: 작은 말다툼이 큰 싸움의 계기가 됐어요.
phrases.en: A small quarrel became the trigger for a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '촉발'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서도 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '촉발' but easy and fine in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: A small quarrel set off a fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '촉발'은 이름처럼 쓰고, '촉발하다'는 동사로 '~을/를 촉발하다' 꼴로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '촉발' is the noun; '촉발하다' is the verb used as 'trigger (something)'.

explain_en: Setting off an event or cause, formal/written (촉발 원인) It is attached to other words, as in '~의 촉발' or '촉발 원인'. The verbs '촉발하다' and '촉발되다' are more common than the noun alone. In daily talk people say '계기'; '촉발' belongs to stiff writing such as news and reports.

t90.ax: That incident was what set off the protest.

examples.en: When fatigue builds up, the body starts to hurt.
Accumulated experience creates skill.
Building up data takes a long time.

examples.ko: 지방 축적을 막으려면 운동을 해야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent fat build-up, you need to exercise.

examples.ko: 부의 축적 방법을 다룬 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book about how to accumulate wealth.

examples.ko: 오랜 축적 끝에 이 기술이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This technology came after a long period of accumulation.

explain: 조금씩 쌓여서 많아지는 것을 말하며 '피로 축적', '데이터 축적', '경험 축적'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 물건을 쌓는 것은 '쌓다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '축적되다', '축적하다' 형태로 만나요.

phrases.en: Stress builds up in the body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 하지 않아도 저절로 쌓이는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something builds up on its own without someone doing it.

phrases.en: Building up experience develops your skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 그대로 다른 명사 뒤에 붙여 '무엇을 쌓는 일'을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to another noun to name the act of building something up.

phrases.en: Accumulating data takes time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 안 보이는 정보를 오래 모은다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for gradually gathering intangible information over time.

explain_en: Deliberate gathering of experience, knowledge or capital (경험의 축적) The gradual piling up of something, mostly intangible things such as fatigue, data, or experience. For physically stacking objects, '쌓다' is more natural. You will most often meet it as 축적되다 or 축적하다.

examples.ko: 이번 실수는 회사에 치명타가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This mistake could be a fatal blow to the company.
The injury was a devastating blow to that player.

examples.ko: 환율 상승이 수출 업체에 치명타를 안겼어요.
examples.en: The rise in the exchange rate dealt a heavy blow to exporters.
That rumor was a killer blow to the shop.

examples.ko: 한 번의 거짓말이 신뢰에 치명타를 입혔어요.
examples.en: A single lie dealt a fatal blow to trust.
The heavy rain dealt a serious blow to the farms.

explain: '타격'보다 회복하기 어려울 만큼 크고 심한 피해일 때 써요. '치명타를 입다', '치명타를 주다', '치명타가 되다'처럼 자주 말해요. 복싱 같은 경기에서 결정적으로 맞은 한 방을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 주전 선수를 잃고 치명타를 입었어요.
phrases.en: The team took a fatal blow when it lost its star player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 회복하기 어려운 피해를 받았다는 뜻이에요. 피해를 받는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means suffering heavy damage that is hard to recover from; the victim is the subject.

phrases.example: 가격 인상은 작은 가게에 치명타를 줬어요.
phrases.en: The price increase dealt a fatal blow to small shops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 주는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the one causing the damage is the subject.

phrases.example: 한 번의 실수가 시험에서 치명타가 됐어요.
phrases.en: One mistake became a fatal blow in the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 결정적인 큰 손해의 원인이 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something turns out to be the decisive cause of great damage.

explain_en: Figurative devastating blow to plans, business, or morale. Compared with '타격' (a hit), it means damage so serious that recovery is hard. It is often used as '치명타를 입다', '치명타를 주다' or '치명타가 되다'. It can also describe a decisive punch in a sport like boxing.

examples.ko: 여름에는 모기 퇴치 스프레이가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: In summer you really need a mosquito repellent spray.

examples.ko: 정부가 질병 퇴치를 위해 예산을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The government increased its budget to eradicate the disease.
We left the cockroach extermination to a professional company.

examples.ko: 쥐 퇴치에 효과가 좋은 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a method that works well for getting rid of mice.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 잡초 퇴치 작업을 함께 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers worked together on clearing out the weeds.
Eradicating the infectious disease is the biggest goal.

explain: '퇴치'는 모기, 쥐, 병처럼 해로운 것을 없앨 때 써요. 약이나 방법을 말할 때 '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: In spring I get rid of pests at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레처럼 해로운 것을 없애는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to getting rid of harmful bugs.

phrases.example: 여행 갈 때 벌레 퇴치제를 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: I packed bug repellent when I went on a trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레를 없애거나 쫓는 약을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A product used to kill or drive away bugs.

phrases.en: The government is working hard to eradicate disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레뿐 아니라 병을 없애는 일에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for wiping out diseases, not only bugs.

explain_en: Pests, germs, disease; practical removal (모기 퇴치) 퇴치 is used for getting rid of harmful things like mosquitoes, rats or diseases. For a product or method, put the target first: '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'.

t90.ax: In summer you really need a mosquito repellent spray.

en: to improve; to get better; to recover

examples.en: My health improved after I received treatment.
If the economy improves, jobs will increase.
The patient's condition is improving little by little.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 호전될 기미가 보여요.
examples.en: There are signs that the relationship between the two countries will improve.
The weather improved, so the plane took off.
The symptoms have not improved yet.

explain: 병세·상황·경기처럼 나쁘던 것이 좋은 쪽으로 바뀔 때 써요. '좋아지다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스·병원·경제 이야기에 잘 나와요. 반대는 '악화되다'예요.

phrases.en: The patient's condition has improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 뉴스에서 환자 상태가 좋아졌다고 할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in hospitals and news for a patient's condition getting better.

phrases.en: I hope the economy improves soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기를 바라다'를 붙여 상황이 좋아지길 바란다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -기를 바라다 it expresses hope that a situation will improve.

phrases.en: There are no signs of improvement yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기미'는 어떤 일이 일어날 조짐으로, 좋아질 낌새가 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 기미 means a sign; used to say whether there are hints of improvement.

explain_en: Illness or economy turns better by itself. Use it when something bad, like an illness, a situation, or the economy, turns for the better. It is stiffer than 좋아지다 and fits news, hospital, and economy talk. The opposite is 악화되다.

dis.h: illness or economy takes a better turn
gh: skill or level rises; active form

p.n: 좋아졌다 is plainer; 호전되다 is formal or medical.

t90.ax: The symptoms have not improved yet.

en: to spread; to disperse; to diffuse

examples.en: Rumors spread quickly on the internet.
A cold spread through our school.

examples.ko: 새로운 유행이 전 세계로 확산하고 있어요.
examples.en: A new trend is spreading around the world.

examples.ko: 나쁜 소문이 확산하지 않게 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to be careful so bad rumors don't spread.
The medical staff were busy trying to stop the spreading infection.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관이 회사 전체로 확산하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope a good habit spreads across the whole company.

explain: '퍼지다'는 소문, 냄새, 병에 두루 쓰는 일상 말이고, '확산하다'는 뉴스나 보고서에서 범위가 넓어지는 상황에 써요. '확산되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The news spread quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '확산하다'와 같은 뜻으로 많이 쓰고, 저절로 퍼지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the same meaning as 확산하다, with a feeling of spreading by itself.

phrases.en: The smell spread through the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural everyday word.

phrases.en: The trend spreads quickly among students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠르게'를 붙여 퍼지는 속도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 빠르게 describes how fast it spreads.

explain_en: Formal, ideas, fear or problems spread wider (확산하다) 퍼지다 is the everyday word for rumors, smells, and illness; 확산하다 is used in news and reports when the range keeps widening. 확산되다 is also common with the same meaning.

t90.ax: A cold spread through our school.
